doan.khoa: Midnight at the Gibraltar frontier. To walk in from Spain, you cross an airport runway. Since July 2026, this gate has had no routine checks. The Rock sits at the western gate of the Mediterranean. Historians on both sides count fourteen sieges of it, between 1309 and 1783. This is why everyone fought over it, told from both sides' records.
doan.gui: Midnight at the Gibraltar frontier. To walk in from Spain, you cross an airport runway. Since July twenty twenty-six, this gate has had no routine checks. The Rock sits at the western gate of the Mediterranean. Historians on both sides count fourteen sieges of it, between thirteen oh-nine and seventeen eighty-three. This is why everyone fought over it, told from both sides' records.

doan.khoa: Four days later, the French and Spanish fleets gathered in the bay: forty-seven ships of the line by the British count, fifty by the Spanish. The Duc de Crillon led the siege. Their answer to red-hot shot: ten floating batteries, designed by the French engineer d'Arçon. A French account says he'd asked to test them against red-hot shot first. It was refused. The thirteenth of September 1782. That morning, the batteries moved into position under the garrison's fire. At ten twenty-five, by the Spanish account, the attackers' guns, some four hundred, opened fire together. By the next afternoon, all ten batteries were lost. Over two thousand attackers were lost, by a British estimate that includes prisoners, and by a Spanish one; the British rescued three hundred and fifty-seven.
